analysis:
Examined all eight batch analyses and the available replayed patches/metadata against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. No concrete regression is independently established. Replay omits 27 of 34 reviewed source units, materially limiting integration verification.

MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift:1024-1035 excludes distributed pairs and logprobs from thought-loop recovery. Its new second-row submission (:1108-1169) explicitly retains request cache scope, cache enablement and donation demand, supporting T-041 isolation; no cache-storage, encryption or attestation change is demonstrated. GenerationLoopExitThinking.swift:108-129 validates the closing token and creates request-local recording; :38-54 adds generated-token retention. GenerationLoopGuardPolicy.swift:83-87 wires the exit policy into the guard. Reported constrained-output exclusions are not independently verifiable from the replayed patch's surrounding source.

Remaining material checks: inspect LoopExitThinkingContinuation.swift:108-230 together with bridge admission and terminal consumers to confirm aggregate output/context bounds, cancellation during row retirement/resubmission (T-010, A-018), and usage accounting across both rows (A-009). The continuation submission omits the original usage signal, token constraint and service reservation; those omissions alone do not establish bypasses, because eligibility, splice accounting and bridge enforcement are outside replay. Verify error-derived outcome logging at scheduler :1162-1166 cannot disclose prompt content (A-001).

For cluster changes, analyses describe stop-generation forwarding in ClusterControlLeadership.swift:828-878 and guarded starts in ClusterOnboardingLive.swift:1517-1527,1699-1702. Their implementation is not replayed. Inspect these with ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift:2901-3539 to verify capture-before-await, authoritative atomic stop comparison, registration restarts and leader changes. Preserve authorization and add-on admission controls (T-053, T-059). Added tests describe intended lifecycle and continuation behavior, but cannot resolve these omitted production contracts. Further review should target these PR-specific uncertainties, not unrelated unchanged implementations.
